proposed_status_reason: Cap rate 4.3% (base case) is well below 10% threshold. Even under highly optimistic assumptions (highest rent estimate $550/mo, lowest HOA estimate $80/mo, self-management, zero other expenses), cap rate reaches only 8.9%. The fundamental issue is that gross yield (10.09% at Scout's $500/mo estimate) was barely at threshold; once operating expenses are factored in, the property cannot achieve 10%+ cap rate under any reasonable scenario. Additionally, HOA and special assessments remain UNKNOWN, adding material uncertainty to an already unfavorable analysis.
underwriting_notes: The property's gross yield appeared promising at Scout stage (~10.1%), but detailed analysis reveals operating expenses consume roughly 55% of rental income. Key issues: (1) HOA fee is UNKNOWN - building has 13 premium amenities including pool, spa, gym, cinema, coworking space, and 24/7 security/concierge, suggesting fees likely toward upper range ($120-150/mo). (2) The low purchase price ($59,444) cannot compensate for the expense load relative to achievable rents. (3) Even assuming $0 HOA (impossible given amenities), cap rate would only be 6.7%. Recommend archiving for future rescreen if HOA fees become known or if significant price reduction occurs.
